# Справка AlphaXiv: mcp

Сохранённая внешняя документация. Копия адаптирована для переносимости: локальные пути и демонстрационные реквизиты/объекты заменены параметрами; содержимое не является конфигурацией готового аккаунта. Она описывает продукты, версии и варианты доступа, а не состояние какого-либо аккаунта. Примеры ОС, тарифов, путей и лимитов выбираются по целевой установке; числовые условия проверяются у поставщика перед использованием. Даты и исходная терминология могут относиться к версии справки.

<div class="header border-b border-border pb-8">

# MCP Server

The alphaXiv Model Context Protocol (MCP) server gives AI applications, agents, and workflows programmatic access to our research corpus. Search and read papers, analyze PDFs, explore paper codebases, find the researchers behind the work, and manage your library — all through native MCP tools.

</div>

<div class="section mt-10">

## Getting started

Endpoint  
<span class="flex items-center gap-1.5">`https://api.alphaxiv.org/mcp/v1`<img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," class="lucide lucide-copy size-4 shrink-0 cursor-pointer text-subtext hover:text-text" /></span>

Transport  
Streamable HTTP (POST for requests, GET for server→client SSE stream, DELETE to terminate)

Authentication  
By default the server advertises OAuth 2.1: your MCP client opens a browser sign-in on first use and refreshes tokens on its own. No configuration needed.\
\
For non-interactive use (scripts, CI, headless agents), create an API key under Settings \> API Keys and send it as an `Authorization: Bearer <key>` header instead. A request carrying a key skips the OAuth flow entirely, and deleting the key revokes access immediately.

Protocol  
Model Context Protocol (MCP) v1.0.0

Supported clients  
Native MCP clients only — Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, Zed, and CLI bridges like `mcp-remote`.\
\
Browser-hosted MCP integrations (e.g. adding this server directly inside claude.ai or chatgpt.com) are **not supported**, because CORS is locked down to first-party origins.\
To use this server from a browser-based assistant, run a local bridge such as `npx mcp-remote https://api.alphaxiv.org/mcp/v1` and point the assistant at the bridge.

</div>

## Available tools

The server exposes 21 tools across three groups. Combine them to build research workflows that discover, read, and organize papers, and that trace the people behind them.

<div class="mt-8">

### Research tools

Read your feeds, search the corpus, read papers, and explore their code. Feed retrieval is free of assistant quota; the search and analysis tools count against it.

### discover_papers

</div>

</div>

Discovers and ranks multiple candidate papers for a research topic. Internally runs an agentic retrieval loop that combines keyword search, embedding search, and optional multi-round follow-up searches. Best for literature discovery, related work, and broad topical coverage.

<div class="flex flex-col gap-2">

#### Parameters

<div class="divide-y divide-border rounded-lg border border-border">

<div class="px-3 py-2.5">

<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-2 gap-y-1">

`keywords``string[]`<span class="rounded-full bg-custom-red/10 px-2 py-0.5 text-[11px] font-medium text-custom-red">required</span>

</div>

3-4 concise keyword terms for exact-name, acronym, method, benchmark, author, or title matching. Plain text only.

</div>

<div class="px-3 py-2.5">

<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-2 gap-y-1">

`question``string`<span class="rounded-full bg-custom-red/10 px-2 py-0.5 text-[11px] font-medium text-custom-red">required</span>

</div>

A detailed semantic description of the papers that would best answer the user's request. Include the important concepts, methods, applications, and related terms.

</div>

<div class="px-3 py-2.5">

<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-2 gap-y-1">

`difficulty``number (1-10)`<span class="rounded-full bg-custom-red/10 px-2 py-0.5 text-[11px] font-medium text-custom-red">required</span>

</div>

A 1-10 estimate of how much retrieval effort this request warrants. Higher values take longer but trigger multi-round follow-up searches.

</div>

<div class="px-3 py-2.5">

<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-2 gap-y-1">

`published_after``string`<span class="text-xs text-subtext">optional</span>

</div>

Only return papers first published on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD). Omit unless the request names a real boundary; this excludes papers outright.

</div>

<div class="px-3 py-2.5">

<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-2 gap-y-1">

`published_before``string`<span class="text-xs text-subtext">optional</span>

</div>

Only return papers first published on or before this date (YYYY-MM-DD). Omit unless the request names a historical window.

</div>

<div class="px-3 py-2.5">

<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-2 gap-y-1">

`prioritize``"default" | "historical" | "recency"`<span class="text-xs text-subtext">optional</span>

</div>

How to sort and prioritize the results.

</div>

</div>

</div>

<div class="flex flex-col gap-1.5">

#### Returns

Ranked list of 5-15 papers, ordered by the requested priority, with: title, publication date, contributing organizations, abstract preview, and arXiv ID.

</div>

### get_paper_content

</div>

</div>

Get the content of an arXiv/alphaXiv paper as text. By default returns a structured AI-generated intermediate report optimized for LLM consumption. If no report is available, automatically falls back to the full extracted text. Use the fullText option to skip the report and get the raw extracted text directly.

<div class="flex flex-col gap-2">

#### Parameters

<div class="divide-y divide-border rounded-lg border border-border">

<div class="px-3 py-2.5">

<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-2 gap-y-1">

`url``string (URL)`<span class="rounded-full bg-custom-red/10 px-2 py-0.5 text-[11px] font-medium text-custom-red">required</span>

</div>

An arXiv or alphaXiv URL (e.g., 'https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.12307', 'https://arxiv.org/pdf/2401.12345', 'https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2307.12307')

</div>

<div class="px-3 py-2.5">

<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-2 gap-y-1">

`fullText``boolean`<span class="text-xs text-subtext">optional</span>

</div>

If true, return the full extracted text instead of the intermediate report. Defaults to false. Useful when you need raw paper content or the report is insufficient.

</div>

</div>

</div>

<div class="flex flex-col gap-1.5">

#### Returns

The paper content as text. By default, a structured AI-generated report. With fullText=true, the raw extracted text of the paper page by page.

</div>

<div class="flex items-start justify-between gap-3">

<div class="flex min-w-0 items-center gap-2.5">

### answer_pdf_queries

</div>

</div>

Returns the filtered page-level content of a single PDF that is relevant to one or more queries. Output is XML (\<paper id="..."\>\<page num="N"\>...\</page\>...\</paper\>) so you can construct citations directly from the returned page text. To read multiple papers, issue multiple tool calls in parallel. Multiple queries on the same paper are nearly free — batch every question you have for that paper into one call.

<div class="flex flex-col gap-2">

#### Parameters

<div class="divide-y divide-border rounded-lg border border-border">

<div class="px-3 py-2.5">

<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-2 gap-y-1">

`paper``string`<span class="rounded-full bg-custom-red/10 px-2 py-0.5 text-[11px] font-medium text-custom-red">required</span>

</div>

The paper to read, as an ID ('2307.12307'), a URL, or a title. Supports arXiv (arxiv.org/pdf/\*, arxiv.org/abs/\*), alphaXiv (alphaxiv.org/abs/\*), Semantic Scholar abstract pages, and direct PDF URLs. A title is resolved to a single best match, reported back in the \<paper\> tag.

</div>

<div class="px-3 py-2.5">

<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-2 gap-y-1">

`queries``string[]`<span class="rounded-full bg-custom-red/10 px-2 py-0.5 text-[11px] font-medium text-custom-red">required</span>

</div>

One or more brief descriptions of the information you're looking for in the paper. Batch all questions about a paper into a single call.

</div>

</div>

</div>

<div class="flex flex-col gap-1.5">

#### Returns

XML containing only the pages relevant to your queries: \<paper id="..."\>\<page num="N"\>page text\</page\>...\</paper\>. Use the page text directly to construct citations.

</div>

<img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," class="lucide lucide-chevron-right size-4 text-subtext transition-transform group-open:rotate-90" />Examples<span class="text-xs font-normal text-subtext">(3)</span>

<div class="mt-3 flex flex-col gap-4">

<div class="flex flex-col gap-2">

Ask about a single aspect of the paper

<div class="markdown-content">

<div id="read_files_from_github_repository" class="flex scroll-mt-24 flex-col gap-4 py-8 first:pt-0 last:pb-0">

### read_files_from_github_repository

</div>

</div>

Reads the contents of files or directories from a paper's GitHub repository. This tool has special behaviors for efficient code exploration: reading '/' returns the complete file tree and all top-level files; reading a directory fetches all files in parallel; reading a file returns its contents.

<div class="flex flex-col gap-2">

#### Parameters

<div class="divide-y divide-border rounded-lg border border-border">

<div class="px-3 py-2.5">

<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-2 gap-y-1">

`githubUrl``string (URL)`<span class="rounded-full bg-custom-red/10 px-2 py-0.5 text-[11px] font-medium text-custom-red">required</span>

</div>

The URL of the paper's codebase repository (e.g., https://github.com/owner/repo)

</div>

<div class="px-3 py-2.5">

<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-2 gap-y-1">

`path``string`<span class="rounded-full bg-custom-red/10 px-2 py-0.5 text-[11px] font-medium text-custom-red">required</span>

</div>

The path to the file or directory. Use '/' to get the entire repository structure and top-level files.

</div>

</div>

</div>

<div class="flex flex-col gap-1.5">

#### Returns

For files: the file contents as text. For directories: list of files/directories with their contents fetched in parallel. For '/': complete file tree plus all top-level file contents.

</div>

<div class="mt-8">

### Researcher tools

Find people rather than papers: who works on a subject, an organization's roster, where someone is now, and who they publish with. Researchers are addressed by the slug rendered at /@slug, and get_researcher, get_researcher_papers, and resolve_researchers also accept plain names and resolve them for you. The search and profile tools count against your assistant quota; the follow tools do not.

<div class="mt-4 divide-y divide-border">

<div id="find_researchers" class="flex scroll-mt-24 flex-col gap-4 py-8 first:pt-0 last:pb-0">

<div class="flex items-start justify-between gap-3">

<div class="flex min-w-0 items-center gap-2.5">

<span class="shrink-0 text-custom-red"><img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," class="lucide lucide-users size-5" /></span>

### find_researchers

</div>

</div>

Finds researchers by subject, organization, career history, or coauthorship. A topic query is answered from the authorship graph rather than from profile text, so it reaches the people who publish on a subject rather than only those who describe themselves that way. Composable with current affiliation, role, citation range, and dated position filters.

<div class="flex flex-col gap-2">

#### Parameters

<div class="divide-y divide-border rounded-lg border border-border">

<div class="px-3 py-2.5">

<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-2 gap-y-1">

`query``string`<span class="text-xs text-subtext">optional</span>

</div>

A person's name when identifying that person is the task, or a research subject. Omit for structured roster and career queries.

</div>

<div class="px-3 py-2.5">

<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-2 gap-y-1">

`topic``string`<span class="text-xs text-subtext">optional</span>

</div>

Research subject answered from paper authorship, for 'who works on X'. Use one concept in the vocabulary its own papers use; concatenating related concepts matches none of them.

</div>

<div class="px-3 py-2.5">

<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-2 gap-y-1">

`topic_authors``"lead" | "senior" | "any"`<span class="text-xs text-subtext">optional</span>

</div>

Which byline slot topic weights: lead for the students and postdocs driving the work, senior for the PIs closing the author list. Defaults to lead.

</div>

<div class="px-3 py-2.5">

<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-2 gap-y-1">

`affiliation``string`<span class="text-xs text-subtext">optional</span>

</div>

Current organization. Every indexed spelling of it is matched, so write the name plainly rather than spelling out variants.

</div>

<div class="px-3 py-2.5">

<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-2 gap-y-1">

`include_past_affiliations``boolean`<span class="text-xs text-subtext">optional</span>

</div>

Shorthand for a past position at affiliation, excluding researchers whose current affiliation still matches. Defaults to false.

</div>

<div class="px-3 py-2.5">

<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-2 gap-y-1">

`position``object`<span class="text-xs text-subtext">optional</span>

</div>

Career-history filter. Affiliation, role, status, and every date bound apply to the same position row.

</div>

<div class="px-3 py-2.5">

<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-2 gap-y-1">

`relationship``object`<span class="text-xs text-subtext">optional</span>

</div>

Coauthorship evidence against an anchor researcher: shared papers, what share of that person's own output the collaboration is, and how often they lead a paper the anchor closes.

</div>

<div class="px-3 py-2.5">

<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-2 gap-y-1">

`role``string`<span class="text-xs text-subtext">optional</span>

</div>

Current role, token-matched ('professor' matches assistant and associate professors). Only current roles are indexed.

</div>

<div class="px-3 py-2.5">

<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-2 gap-y-1">

`min_citations``number`<span class="text-xs text-subtext">optional</span>

</div>

Citation floor, to keep a roster to established researchers.

</div>

<div class="px-3 py-2.5">

<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-2 gap-y-1">

`max_citations``number`<span class="text-xs text-subtext">optional</span>

</div>

Citation ceiling, to find rising researchers who are not yet famous.

</div>

<div class="px-3 py-2.5">

<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-2 gap-y-1">

`sort``"relevance" | "citations" | "recent_activity" | "relationship_strength"`<span class="text-xs text-subtext">optional</span>

</div>

Result ordering. A topic search carries its own ranking and ignores this. Defaults to relevance.

</div>

<div class="px-3 py-2.5">

<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-2 gap-y-1">

`limit``number (1-100)`<span class="text-xs text-subtext">optional</span>

</div>

Results per page. Defaults to 12, or 50 for a relationship search.

</div>

<div class="px-3 py-2.5">

<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-2 gap-y-1">

`page``number`<span class="text-xs text-subtext">optional</span>

</div>

1-based page over the same ordering, defaulting to 1. Every result says whether more matched beyond it.

</div>

</div>

</div>

<div class="flex flex-col gap-1.5">

#### Returns

Ranked researchers with a \[SLUG=...\] handle, name, current position, citations, and the evidence behind the match. A topic search also returns the defining papers on that topic and who wrote them.

</div>

Who someone publishes with

<div id="get_researcher" class="flex scroll-mt-24 flex-col gap-4 py-8 first:pt-0 last:pb-0">

<div class="flex items-start justify-between gap-3">

<div class="flex min-w-0 items-center gap-2.5">

<span class="shrink-0 text-custom-red"><img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," class="lucide lucide-user-round size-5" /></span>

### get_researcher

</div>

</div>

Gets compact profiles for up to 25 researchers at once. Names resolve to the best-matching indexed researcher and tolerate a misspelling, so a slug is never required. Current positions and up to five curated past positions are returned by default; everything else is opt-in.

<div class="flex flex-col gap-2">

#### Parameters

<div class="divide-y divide-border rounded-lg border border-border">

<div class="px-3 py-2.5">

<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-2 gap-y-1">

`researchers``string[] (1-25)`<span class="rounded-full bg-custom-red/10 px-2 py-0.5 text-[11px] font-medium text-custom-red">required</span>

</div>

Full names or exact slugs. A corrected spelling is reported inline.

</div>

<div class="px-3 py-2.5">

<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-2 gap-y-1">

`include``string[]`<span class="text-xs text-subtext">optional</span>

</div>

Additional sections: bio, position_history, linkedin_experience, education, citation_trajectory, coauthors, alphaxiv_account, links.

</div>

<div class="px-3 py-2.5">

<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-2 gap-y-1">

`papers``"none" | "notable" | "recent"`<span class="text-xs text-subtext">optional</span>

</div>

Optional paper context for small profiles. For a larger or date-bounded paper question use get_researcher_papers instead. Defaults to none.

</div>

<div class="px-3 py-2.5">

<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-2 gap-y-1">

`paper_limit``number (1-10)`<span class="text-xs text-subtext">optional</span>

</div>

Papers per researcher when papers is set. Defaults to 3.

</div>

</div>

</div>

<div class="flex flex-col gap-1.5">

#### Returns

One profile per researcher: slug, name, current and past positions, citation metrics, and each requested section.

</div>

<img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," class="lucide lucide-chevron-right size-4 text-subtext transition-transform group-open:rotate-90" />Examples<span class="text-xs font-normal text-subtext">(2)</span>

<div id="get_researcher_papers" class="flex scroll-mt-24 flex-col gap-4 py-8 first:pt-0 last:pb-0">

<div class="flex items-start justify-between gap-3">

<div class="flex min-w-0 items-center gap-2.5">

### get_researcher_papers

</div>

</div>

The papers on alphaXiv for one or many researchers, grouped per researcher. Sort by recent with published_after to answer what someone is working on now, or by cited for their best-known work. Returned paper ids chain into the paper tools.

<div class="flex flex-col gap-2">

#### Parameters

<div class="divide-y divide-border rounded-lg border border-border">

<div class="px-3 py-2.5">

<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-2 gap-y-1">

`researchers``string[] (1-25)`<span class="rounded-full bg-custom-red/10 px-2 py-0.5 text-[11px] font-medium text-custom-red">required</span>

</div>

Full names or exact slugs, resolved the same way as get_researcher.

</div>

<div class="px-3 py-2.5">

<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-2 gap-y-1">

`sort``"recent" | "cited" | "viewed"`<span class="text-xs text-subtext">optional</span>

</div>

cited for notable work, recent for current activity, viewed for alphaXiv attention. Defaults to cited.

</div>

<div class="px-3 py-2.5">

<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-2 gap-y-1">

`published_after``string`<span class="text-xs text-subtext">optional</span>

</div>

Only papers first published on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD).

</div>

<div class="px-3 py-2.5">

<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-2 gap-y-1">

`limit_per_researcher``number (1-25)`<span class="text-xs text-subtext">optional</span>

</div>

Papers returned per researcher. Defaults to 10.

</div>

</div>

</div>

<div class="flex flex-col gap-1.5">

#### Returns

Papers per researcher with title, arXiv id, publication date, citations, and views, plus how many of their all-time papers the page covers.

</div>

<div id="resolve_researchers" class="flex scroll-mt-24 flex-col gap-4 py-8 first:pt-0 last:pb-0">

<div class="flex items-start justify-between gap-3">

<div class="flex min-w-0 items-center gap-2.5">

<span class="shrink-0 text-custom-red"><img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," class="lucide lucide-user-search size-5" /></span>

### resolve_researchers

</div>

</div>

Turns a list of people you read somewhere else — a lab roster, a team page, an award list — into current alphaXiv researcher entries, so you cite where someone works now rather than what the page said. Pass every person in one batch. Optional per-person URLs and related researchers disambiguate common names.

<div class="flex flex-col gap-2">

#### Parameters

<div class="divide-y divide-border rounded-lg border border-border">

<div class="px-3 py-2.5">

<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-2 gap-y-1">

`people``object[] (1-50)`<span class="rounded-full bg-custom-red/10 px-2 py-0.5 text-[11px] font-medium text-custom-red">required</span>

</div>

Each entry takes the person's name as printed by the source, plus an optional personal, institutional, Scholar, LinkedIn, or OpenReview url for that person. Do not pass the shared roster URL.

</div>

<div class="px-3 py-2.5">

<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-2 gap-y-1">

`related_researchers``string[] (max 5)`<span class="text-xs text-subtext">optional</span>

</div>

<div class="mt-8">

### Library tools

Manage the folders in your library on your behalf, and edit the metadata of papers you uploaded yourself. Folders are addressed by the opaque folder_id returned from list_library. The default 'Want to read', 'Reading', and 'Completed' folders represent reading status and overlap freely – a paper can live in any number of folders at once.

<div class="mt-4 divide-y divide-border">

<div id="list_library" class="flex scroll-mt-24 flex-col gap-4 py-8 first:pt-0 last:pb-0">

<div class="flex items-start justify-between gap-3">

<div class="flex min-w-0 items-center gap-2.5">

<span class="shrink-0 text-custom-red"><img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," class="lucide lucide-library size-5" /></span>

### list_library

</div>

</div>

Lists the user's folders (bookmark collections) with their folder_id, name, type, parent_id, sharing_status, and paper_count. This is the entry point for every other library tool, since folders are addressed by the folder_id it returns.

<div class="flex flex-col gap-2">

#### Parameters

<div class="divide-y divide-border rounded-lg border border-border">

<div class="px-3 py-2.5">

<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-2 gap-y-1">

`include_papers``boolean`<span class="text-xs text-subtext">optional</span>

</div>

Also list the papers inside each folder (capped per folder), each with its id, title, publication date, and whether it is a public arXiv paper or one the user uploaded. Defaults to false.

</div>

<div class="px-3 py-2.5">

<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-2 gap-y-1">

`paper_ids_or_urls``string[]`<span class="text-xs text-subtext">optional</span>

</div>

Report which folders already contain each of these papers.

</div>

</div>

</div>

<div class="flex flex-col gap-1.5">

#### Returns

The list of folders. With include_papers, each folder also carries its papers. With paper_ids_or_urls, an added paper_membership section maps each paper to the folders that hold it.

</div>

<img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," class="lucide lucide-chevron-right size-4 text-subtext transition-transform group-open:rotate-90" />Examples<span class="text-xs font-normal text-subtext">(2)</span>

<div id="edit_private_paper_metadata" class="flex scroll-mt-24 flex-col gap-4 py-8 first:pt-0 last:pb-0">

<div class="flex items-start justify-between gap-3">

<div class="flex min-w-0 items-center gap-2.5">

<span class="shrink-0 text-custom-red"><img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," class="lucide lucide-file-pen size-5" /></span>

### edit_private_paper_metadata

</div>

<div class="inline-flex items-center rounded-full border px-2.5 py-0.5 text-xs font-semibold transition-colors border-transparent bg-surface text-text hover:bg-surface/80">

Writes

</div>

</div>

Edits the metadata of a paper you uploaded to alphaXiv yourself. Papers from arXiv cannot be edited. Only the fields you pass change; the rest keep their current values. Uploads default to the upload date as their publication date, so this is how an agent that has looked up a paper's real publication date corrects it.

<div class="flex flex-col gap-2">

#### Parameters

<div class="divide-y divide-border rounded-lg border border-border">

<div class="px-3 py-2.5">

<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-2 gap-y-1">

`paper_id_or_url``string`<span class="rounded-full bg-custom-red/10 px-2 py-0.5 text-[11px] font-medium text-custom-red">required</span>

</div>

The paper's id as returned by list_library, or its alphaXiv URL.

</div>

<div class="px-3 py-2.5">

<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-2 gap-y-1">

`title``string`<span class="text-xs text-subtext">optional</span>

</div>

New title.

</div>

<div class="px-3 py-2.5">

<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-2 gap-y-1">

`abstract``string`<span class="text-xs text-subtext">optional</span>

</div>

New abstract.

</div>

<div class="px-3 py-2.5">

<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-2 gap-y-1">

`authors``string[]`<span class="text-xs text-subtext">optional</span>

</div>

Full author names in byline order. Replaces the current list entirely.

</div>

<div class="px-3 py-2.5">

<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-2 gap-y-1">

`publication_date``string`<span class="text-xs text-subtext">optional</span>

</div>

The date the paper was originally published (YYYY-MM-DD), not the date it was uploaded.

</div>

<div class="px-3 py-2.5">

<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-2 gap-y-1">

`categories``string[]`<span class="text-xs text-subtext">optional</span>

</div>

Subject categories such as 'cs.LG'. Replaces the current list entirely.

</div>

<div class="px-3 py-2.5">

<div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-2 gap-y-1">

`bibtex``string | null`<span class="text-xs text-subtext">optional</span>

</div>

BibTeX citation for the paper, or null to clear it.

</div>

</div>

</div>

<div class="flex flex-col gap-1.5">

#### Returns

The paper's metadata as it now stands.

</div>

<div class="section mt-12">

## Common use cases

<div class="mt-4 grid gap-4 md:grid-cols-2">

<div class="flex flex-col gap-3 rounded-xl border border-border p-5">

### <span class="text-custom-red"><img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," class="lucide lucide-book-marked size-5" /></span>Literature Review

1.  1\. Use discover_papers to surface relevant candidates for the topic
2.  2\. Re-run discover_papers with varied keywords/questions or a higher difficulty to fill gaps and ensure comprehensive coverage
3.  3\. Use answer_pdf_queries (batching multiple questions per paper) to extract citation-ready excerpts from each paper
4.  4\. Synthesize findings across papers

</div>

<div class="flex flex-col gap-3 rounded-xl border border-border p-5">

### <span class="text-custom-red"><img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," class="lucide lucide-code-xml size-5" /></span>Code Analysis

1.  1\. Use discover_papers to find the paper of interest
2.  2\. Extract the GitHub URL from results (or from the paper's metadata)
3.  3\. Use read_files_from_github_repository with path="/" for an overview, then drill into specific directories

</div>

<div class="flex flex-col gap-3 rounded-xl border border-border p-5">

### <span class="text-custom-red"><img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," class="lucide lucide-microscope size-5" /></span>Deep Research

1.  1\. Use discover_papers (possibly multiple framings in parallel) to find sources
2.  2\. Use get_paper_content to read full text or the AI-generated report
3.  3\. Use answer_pdf_queries for citation-grade excerpts from specific pages
4.  4\. Use read_files_from_github_repository to verify implementation claims

</div>

<div class="flex flex-col gap-3 rounded-xl border border-border p-5">

### <span class="text-custom-red"><img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," class="lucide lucide-users size-5" /></span>Researcher Discovery

1.  1\. Use find_researchers with a topic to rank the people publishing on it, and read the defining papers it returns alongside them
2.  2\. Use get_researcher for their positions, education, and collaborators
3.  3\. Use get_researcher_papers sorted by recent to see what they are working on now
4.  4\. Use follow_researcher to keep their new papers coming to the feed

</div>

<div class="flex flex-col gap-3 rounded-xl border border-border p-5">

### <span class="text-custom-red"><img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," class="lucide lucide-folder-tree size-5" /></span>Library Management

1.  1\. Use list_library to read the user's folders and their folder_id
2.  2\. Use create_folder to organize a topic, then save_papers_to_folder to fill it
3.  3\. Use move_papers_between_folders to advance papers through reading-status folders as the user reads them
4.  4\. Use edit_private_paper_metadata to fix the publication date or byline of uploaded PDFs, which otherwise carry their upload date

</div>

</div>

</div>

</div>

</div>
